name: Language
dimension: the aspect of language the sentence is about

objects.label: Signal
objects.text: LN.O.A1 Signal

objects.label: Phonetics
objects.text: LN.O.A1.1 Phonetics — articulation, acoustics, perception. Source–filter theory of speech (Fant, 1960) cites PH acoustics.

objects.label: Phonology
objects.text: LN.O.A1.2 Phonology — the phoneme and the minimal pair; distinctive features (Chomsky and Halle, *The Sound Pattern of English*, 1968); Optimality Theory (Prince and Smolensky, 1993).

objects.label: Sign phonology
objects.text: LN.O.A1.3 Sign phonology — handshape, location and movement as parameters (Stokoe, 1960). Sign languages are full natural languages.

objects.label: Writing systems
objects.text: LN.O.A1.4 Writing systems — the IPA is a convention (W12); orthography is not sound.

objects.label: Form
objects.text: LN.O.A2 Form

objects.label: Morphology
objects.text: LN.O.A2.1 Morphology — morphemes; inflection versus derivation.

objects.label: Syntax
objects.text: LN.O.A2.2 Syntax — constituency and recursion; dependency versus phrase structure; agreement.

objects.label: Lexicon
objects.text: LN.O.A2.3 The lexicon — word classes, argument structure.

objects.label: Formal grammars
objects.text: LN.O.A2.4 Formal grammars — the Chomsky hierarchy is MA.O.A1; LN uses it to class natural-language phenomena. Whether natural languages are mildly context-sensitive is CONTESTED.

objects.label: Meaning
objects.text: LN.O.A3 Meaning

objects.label: Lexical semantics
objects.text: LN.O.A3.1 Lexical semantics — sense relations; Saussure's arbitrariness of the sign (*Cours*, 1916).

objects.label: Compositional semantics
objects.text: LN.O.A3.2 Compositional semantics — Frege's principle (concept cited from PL); Montague grammar.

objects.label: Pragmatics
objects.text: LN.O.A3.3 Pragmatics — Grice's cooperative principle and implicature (concept PL, empirical patterns LN); presupposition; deixis; politeness.

objects.label: Grammaticalised meaning
objects.text: LN.O.A3.4 Grammaticalised meaning — e.g. te reo Māori pronouns distinguish dual from plural, and inclusive from exclusive.

objects.label: Variation in use
objects.text: LN.O.A4 Variation in use

objects.label: Social variation
objects.text: LN.O.A4.1 Social variation — the sociolinguistic variable (Labov, 1966).

objects.label: Register and genre
objects.text: LN.O.A4.2 Register and genre — situational variation; diglossia (Ferguson, 1959).

objects.label: Contact and multilingualism
objects.text: LN.O.A4.3 Contact and multilingualism — code-switching; pidgins and creoles.

objects.label: Endangerment and revitalisation
objects.text: LN.O.A4.4 Endangerment and revitalisation — language shift. Te reo Māori: kōhanga reo from 1982; the Māori Language Act 1987 made it an official language of New Zealand.

objects.label: Diversity
objects.text: LN.O.A5 Diversity

objects.label: Change
objects.text: LN.O.A5.1 Change — regular sound change (the Neogrammarian hypothesis, 1870s); Grimm's law (1822); Verner's law (1875); grammaticalisation.

objects.label: Descent and families
objects.text: LN.O.A5.2 Descent and families — the comparative method; Proto-Indo-European; Austronesian, which includes te reo Māori.

objects.label: Typology and universals
objects.text: LN.O.A5.3 Typology and universals — Greenberg's universals (1963), most of them statistical tendencies rather than exceptionless laws.

objects.label: Origin of language
objects.text: LN.O.A5.4 Origin of language — OPEN.

warrants.defeaters: truth-value and felicity judgements in controlled contexts

sections.governing_thought:
Language is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five aspects of language: signal, form, meaning, variation in use, and diversity.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the aspect of language the sentence is about.** Order: from the signal to the family of languages.
1. Signal
2. Form
3. Meaning
4. Variation in use
5. Diversity

A particular language is a catalogue entry on the same five cells. There is no "exotic languages" bucket.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. The system is linguistics; the process is mind (MS).
2. Meaning as a concept is PL; meaning in a language is LN.
3. Formal languages are MA; their use to class natural languages is LN.
4. Language models are CS; whether their outputs show a grammatical generalisation is LN.
5. The poem is AR; the metrical phonology it uses is LN.
6. A scripture's doctrinal sense is RE; its grammar is LN.
7. A word in te reo is LN; its tradition-internal meaning in tikanga is IK.
